title: Everything is down
text: Your service has been unavailable for six hours. Customers are posting screenshots.

opts.label: Full transparency and credits
opts.hint: Publish the post-mortem, refund the day.

out.text: It happens again a month later, and now there is a pattern.
Nobody cares whose fault it was.

lesson: Incidents are inevitable; how you handle them is a choice. Reliability engineering shifts the odds, and honesty limits the damage.

title: Your best team wants out
text: Five of your strongest people in {city} have an idea and want to start a company around it.

opts.label: Fund them as a spin-off
opts.hint: Back them for a 30% stake. You lose the team, keep a share of the upside.

out.text: They leave with your blessing and your money.
They take some knowledge with them.

lesson: Talented people have options. You can share the upside with them inside the company, outside it, or not at all — and they will remember which.

title: News from the spin-off
text: The team you backed two years ago has reached the end of its first chapter.

out.text: They have been acquired. Your stake pays handsomely.
They ran out of money. The stake is worthless.

lesson: Most venture bets fail; a few pay for all the rest. One bet is a lottery ticket, not a strategy.

title: People are running on empty
text: Sick days are up, tempers are short, and two managers have asked what the plan is.

opts.label: Mandatory time off
opts.hint: Close for a week. Lose the output.

out.text: Help is on the way, in a quarter or two.

opts.label: Push through
opts.hint: It is a busy period. It will pass.

out.text: Several people resign in the same week.

lesson: Running people above capacity borrows from the future. Watch utilisation: sustained above 95% it shows up as attrition and quality problems.

title: Someone has been stealing
text: Finance has found a pattern of fake supplier invoices going back two years. It leads to a trusted manager.

opts.label: Quiet dismissal
opts.hint: Recover what you can and say nothing.

out.text: It leaks, along with the fact you hid it.

opts.label: Tighten controls everywhere
opts.hint: Dual sign-off on everything, for ever.

lesson: Internal controls feel like bureaucracy until the day they are missing. Fraud grows where one person can both approve and pay.

title: A complaint about a star
text: Three people have made a formal complaint about the behaviour of {person}, your {role}.

out.text: The investigation clears them, and people accept it.
It goes away. People notice that it went away.
The complainants leave. Others update their CVs.

lesson: Culture is defined by what you tolerate from your best performers. Everyone is watching what happens next.

title: It is in the press
text: A journalist has the whole story of how the complaint was handled, with documents.

opts.label: Apologise and act
opts.hint: Admit it was wrong and change the process.

out.text: The documents are published in full.

lesson: Problems buried rarely stay buried, and the cover-up is always a second story.

title: Water everywhere
text: A burst main has flooded your {city} premises. Nothing will work there for weeks.

opts.label: Rent emergency space
opts.hint: Pay whatever it takes to be running next week.

lesson: Business continuity planning is dull until the day it is the only thing that matters.

title: The systems are creaking
text: The software that runs your operations was built for a company a tenth your size. It fell over twice last month.

opts.label: Migrate now
opts.hint: Two painful quarters, then it is done.

out.text: You move on to other things.

lesson: Technical debt accrues interest. You can pay it down on your schedule or its own.

title: The system finally fell over
text: The old platform has failed completely. Orders are being taken on paper.

out.text: Twice the cost of doing it properly, and a wrecked quarter.

lesson: Deferring a necessary cost does not avoid it. It adds a penalty and lets the timing be chosen for you.

title: An idea from the floor
text: Someone on the front line in {city} thinks they can cut a step out of the main process.

opts.label: Pilot it
opts.hint: Try it in one team first.

out.text: It works. They are thrilled to be listened to.
It does not pan out, but people are glad you tried.

lesson: Small experiments are cheap options: limited downside, real information. Rolling out untested is paying full price for the same lottery ticket.

title: Where should people work?
text: Leases are up for renewal and the question cannot be put off: office, home, or both.

out.text: Some of your best people resign rather than commute.
Costs fall and so, slowly, does cohesion.

lesson: There is no free option here: each trades cost, talent pool and cohesion differently. Know which one your strategy depends on.

title: A vendor doubles its price
text: The supplier of a system you cannot run without has been bought by private equity. The renewal quote has doubled.

opts.label: Switch vendors
opts.hint: A risky migration to a cheaper alternative.

out.text: They call your bluff and cut service during the dispute.

lesson: Switching costs are someone else’s pricing power. The time to negotiate is before you are locked in.

title: You are exhausted
text: You have not had a week off since you started. Your decisions are getting worse and you know it.

out.text: The company runs fine. That is good news.

opts.label: Hire a chief of staff
opts.hint: Someone to carry part of the load.

lesson: A company that cannot run without its founder has a key-person problem at the very top.

title: A decision made at 2 a.m.
text: A contract you signed without reading properly has turned out to mean what it says.
lesson: Judgement is a resource that depletes. Tired leaders make expensive mistakes.

title: Staff are organising
text: A majority of your people in {city} have signed cards to form a union.

opts.label: Address the grievances directly
opts.hint: Raise pay in the office and fix what they are angry about.

out.text: The vote passes anyway, and now you are the villain.

lesson: Union drives are a symptom. The underlying condition is pay, respect or security that people no longer expect to get by asking.

title: New hires are floundering
text: You have hired fast. Managers say half the newcomers still do not know how things work here.

opts.label: Build proper onboarding
opts.hint: A month of structured training for every new hire.

out.text: New people become useful in half the time.

opts.label: Slow the hiring
opts.hint: Absorb the people you have first.

lesson: Hiring faster than you can absorb dilutes skill and culture. Headcount is not capacity until people are productive.

title: A fault reached customers
text: A defect got past your checks in {city} and customers found it before you did.

opts.label: Make everyone whole
opts.hint: Recall, replace, refund — before being asked.

opts.label: Fix it for those who complain

lesson: The cost of a defect multiplies at every stage it survives. Being seen to fix it generously is the cheapest option left once it is out.

title: The credits have run out
text: Your cloud provider has sent the renewal quote. It is not the price you were paying before the credits.

out.text: The migration takes two quarters of engineering.

lesson: This is what lock-in costs.

title: The landlord wants more
text: The lease on your busiest {city} location is up. The landlord wants 60% more rent, knowing you have nowhere else to go on that street.

opts.label: Sign
opts.hint: Keep the best site in town.

opts.label: Move to a cheaper street
opts.hint: Lose some walk-in trade, save the rent.

out.text: The move costs a quarter of disruption.
He lets a rival sign instead.

lesson: Location-dependent businesses carry landlord risk. A long lease is protection and an obligation at the same time.

title: Holiday rush
text: The busiest season of the year is coming. Your managers need to know how many temporary staff to hire.

out.text: Every customer served, a lot of idle temps in the quiet hours.

opts.label: Run lean
opts.hint: The regular team can handle it.

out.text: Queues, tired staff, but a good margin.

lesson: Seasonal demand forces a trade-off between lost sales and idle cost. The right answer depends on your margin per extra sale.

title: No drivers
text: Half your vacancies for drivers have been open three months. Trucks are parked for want of people to drive them.

opts.label: Raise driver pay 10%
opts.hint: The market rate has moved; move with it.

opts.label: Fund a driving school
opts.hint: Train your own; they stay longer.

out.text: A pipeline of new drivers in two quarters.

lesson: When a labour market is tight, the price of labour is set by the market, not by you. Fighting it costs more than paying it.

title: The grid says no
text: On sunny, windy days the grid operator in {region} is ordering your plants to switch off. Power you could sell is going to waste.

opts.label: Add storage
opts.hint: Batteries to shift output to the evening.

out.text: A tenth of your output is curtailed.

lesson: Intermittent assets are only as valuable as the grid’s ability to take their output. Storage and location decide realised value.

title: Too many people on the bench
text: A third of your consultants have no billable work this month. The pipeline looks thin.

out.text: The bench empties at lower rates.

opts.label: Invest the time
opts.hint: Train them and build reusable methods.

lesson: Utilisation is the profit lever in professional services. Discounting to fill capacity trains clients to expect discounts.

title: Promotion round
text: Your best managers expect to make partner this year. There are more candidates than there is partner economics to go round.

out.text: Delight now; partner economics thin out.

opts.label: Up or out
opts.hint: Promote the best, help the rest leave.

lesson: The partnership pyramid depends on growth: without enough new work, promotions dilute the people already at the top.

title: Contamination at your contract manufacturer
text: The contract manufacturer that makes your product has found contamination in a production lot.

out.text: A second source in two quarters.

opts.label: Wait for them to fix it
opts.hint: They are the best in the field.

lesson: Outsourced production moves the work, not the risk.

title: Heatwave
text: Record temperatures across {region}. Air conditioning is failing and people are working half-days.
lesson: Climate is an operating condition now. Productivity, morale and safety all move with the thermometer.

title: Two of your leaders are at war
text: Your heads of sales and of operations no longer speak. Their teams have picked sides.

opts.label: Mediate
opts.hint: Lock them in a room until they agree.

opts.label: Pick a side
opts.hint: Back the one with the better argument.

out.text: The other team feels the loss.

lesson: Conflict between functions is often a conflict between incentives. Change the incentives and the people follow.

title: Layoff rumours
text: A rumour that layoffs are coming is racing through the company. It is not true.

out.text: Some of your best people take recruiter calls.

lesson: In the absence of information people assume the worst. Transparency is cheaper than attrition.

title: The union’s first contract
text: The union in {city} has tabled its demands for a first contract: more pay, set hours, and a say in how work is assigned.

opts.label: Sign a three-year deal
opts.hint: Peace, at a price you can plan for.

out.text: Done. Costs are higher but certain.

opts.label: Tie raises to productivity
opts.hint: A deal that pays for itself, if the productivity comes.

out.text: Talks drag; a short strike before the deal.

opts.label: Refuse and wait them out
opts.hint: The side that can wait longer usually wins.

out.text: A two-month strike, then a deal on worse terms for everyone.
The union backs down. The resentment does not.

lesson: A contract turns labour costs from a fight every year into a number you can plan around. Strikes are expensive for both sides, which is why most end in a deal both could have signed earlier.
